Visit note | 2025-12-02 04:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Sabina Patwary, 27, female. Ms. Patwary attends for her first visit complaining of severe lower abdominal pain and painful cramps during the first few days of each menstrual cycle, which frequently cause her to miss work or classes. She mentions that these symptoms have grown progressively worse since she started a new job involving long standing hours in Uttara. She works as an electrician. She has no chronic comorbidities. Systemic inquiry is otherwise unremarkable. On examination: pain score 9/10, BP 123/83 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 58 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild tenderness in the suprapubic region with no guarding or rebound tenderness. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, engage in light exercise, and keep a detailed period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Mr. Bepari visits the clinic for the first time complaining of severe skin itching that becomes markedly worse in humid weather, accompanied by an enlarging skin rash. He notes that the rash began during the humid monsoon season in Old Dhaka and has developed spreading active edges over the past few weeks. He works as a madrasa teacher, which requires him to sit in crowded classrooms for long hours. He reports no known systemic comorbidities like diabetes or hypertension. He denies any recent travel or exposure to new chemical soaps. General physical examination is unremarkable. Cutaneous examination reveals a well-defined annular erythematous plaque with elevated, scaly borders located on his torso, measuring approximately 5 cm across. The surrounding skin is slightly hyperpigmented from chronic scratching. There are no signs of secondary bacterial infection or regional lymphadenopathy. Systemic review reveals normal cardiovascular and respiratory findings. On examination: affected area about 5 cm across, BP 131/81 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 96 kg. Assessment: Tinea corporis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep his skin dry, avoid sharing towels with family members, and wash all personal clothes in hot water. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
